items.followUp: State the law of conservation of mass.

rubric.why: The law states that energy cannot be created or destroyed.
rubric.description: States that energy can neither be created nor destroyed.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for this conservation statement.

rubric.why: The law allows energy to change from one form to another.
rubric.description: States that energy can be transformed or converted from one form to another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the change of energy from one form to another.

modelAnswer: Energy can neither be created nor destroyed.
It can only be transformed from one form into another, so the total energy remains constant.

items.followUp: A mass of 2 kg occupies a volume of 0.002 m³. Calculate its density.

rubric.why: The given mass is 5 kg, and 5 L converts to 0.005 m³ in SI units.
rubric.description: Identifies the mass and converts the volume to SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating m = 5 kg and V = 0.005 m³.

rubric.why: Density is mass divided by volume; substituting the given values gives 1000 kg/m³.
rubric.description: Uses the density formula and gives the correct density with its SI unit.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula and answer with unit.

modelAnswer: Given: mass, m = 5 kg; volume, V = 5 L = 0.005 m³.
